The petitioners are accused Nos.1 to 3 in C.C.No.130 of 2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Malappuram.

sentences.text:
The offences alleged against them are under Sections 498A and 406 read with Section 34 of the IPC.
2.
The prosecution case is that the 1st petitioner, who married the defacto complainant / 2nd respondent on 08.10.2017, had been subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty, demanding more dowry.

The 2nd petitioner, who is the mother of the 1st petitioner and the 3rd petitioner, who is his sister, are also alleged to have joined the 1st petitioner in perpetrating the aforesaid cruelty upon the defacto complainant.
The case was registered by the Malappuram Vanitha Police Station on 05.05.2023.
After the completion of the investigation, the Sub Inspector of Police, Malappuram Vanitha Police Station, filed the Final Report alleging the commission of the aforesaid offences by the accused.
In the present petition, the petitioners would contend that they are totally innocent, and that they are falsely implicated in this case.
It is further contended that none of the offences alleged are attracted in the facts and circumstances of the case.
According to the petitioners, there are only vague and superficial allegations, which are not sufficient to initiate prosecution proceedings against them.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.

5. A reading of the First Information Statement, as well as the further statement given by the defacto complainant to the Investigating Officer, would reveal that she was subjected to persistent Ibrahim vs State Of Kerala on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71778403/
2 physical and mental torture by the 1st petitioner, demanding more dowry.

However, as against petitioners 2 and 3, there are only vague and superficial allegations to the effect that they used to insult the defacto complainant by innuendos stating the insufficiency of dowry, which she brought from her parents.

Apart from omnibus allegations to the effect that petitioners 2 and 3 joined the 1st petitioner in mentally torturing the defacto complainant for 2025:KER:58770 her failure to bring more money and gold ornaments, there is absolutely no material to fasten petitioners 2 and 3 with the crime alleged in this case.

In the above circumstances, the contention of the petitioners that there are only superficial and vague allegations with regard to the commission of the crime, has to be accepted, insofar as it relates to petitioners 2 and 3.
However, as against the 1st petitioner, it is not possible to say that the allegations levelled by the defacto complainant would not constitute the offences under Sections 498A and 406 IPC.
As a conclusion to the above discussion, I find that the prayer in this petition is liable to be allowed in part, terminating the prosecution proceedings as against petitioners 2 and 3.

In the result, the petition stands allowed in part as follows:
The proceedings against petitioners 2 and 3 (accused Nos.2 and 3) in C.C.No.130 of 2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Malappuram, which arose out of Crime No.35 of 2023 of the Malappuram Vanitha Police Station, are hereby quashed.
It is made clear that there is absolutely no legal impediment for 2025:KER:58770 the learned Magistrate to proceed with the trial as against the 1st accused in that case.
